title: Cordelia Cruises Eyes Mangaluru as Next Port of Call in Fleet Expansion Push
excerpt: Waterways Leisure Tourism, India's only listed domestic cruise operator, is evaluating New Mangalore Port for future cruise services as it prepares to nearly triple fleet capacity by 2028.
body:
• Waterways Leisure Tourism (Cordelia Cruises) has identified New Mangalore Port as a future embarkation point as part of its fleet expansion strategy.
  • The company is adding two vessels — Cordelia Sky (October 2026) and Cordelia Sun (2027) — to its existing MV Empress, nearly tripling passenger capacity.
  • New Mangalore Port is independently experiencing a resurgence in international cruise traffic, with its strongest season since before the pandemic.
  • The expansion aligns with India's Cruise Bharat Mission, which aims to develop 27 new cruise terminals and triple cruise passenger volumes by 2030.

Waterways Leisure Tourism, the company behind India's Cordelia Cruises brand, is exploring the launch of cruise services from Mangaluru as it pursues an aggressive fleet expansion that will see its capacity nearly triple within two years.

The recently listed cruise operator — which debuted on the BSE and NSE on July 1 after raising ₹585 crore through its IPO — has identified New Mangalore Port among several Indian ports it plans to add to its network, according to company disclosures. Other ports under consideration include Kolkata, Porbandar, Port Blair, and Diu Island.

Fleet Expansion Unlocks New Routes

Cordelia currently operates a single vessel, the 35-year-old MV Empress, with a capacity of 2,005 guests across 796 cabins. The company follows a seasonal deployment model, sailing from Mumbai along the western coast from October through June, and shifting to Chennai for Sri Lanka routes during the monsoon months.

That is about to change. Cordelia Sky, a 2,004-guest vessel formerly known as Norwegian Sky, is scheduled to enter service in October 2026. A sister ship, Cordelia Sun (formerly Norwegian Sun, 1,936 guests), will follow in 2027. Together, the three vessels will give the company roughly 5,945 berths — a transformation from a single-ship operator into a multi-vessel fleet.

"One ship was proof of concept. Three ships... is a fleet."

— Jurgen Bailom, President and CEO, Cordelia Cruises

Under the planned repositioning, Cordelia Sky will initially take over Mumbai itineraries while MV Empress shifts to Kochi. Once Cordelia Sun arrives, a three-port network will take shape: Sun operating from Mumbai, Sky from Kochi, and Empress from Chennai on a near year-round basis.

It is within this expanded network that Mangaluru enters the picture. The faster speed capabilities of the newer vessels provide greater flexibility to add intermediate ports to existing itineraries, and New Mangalore's position on the western seaboard — between Mumbai, Goa, and Kochi — makes it a natural addition.

Mangaluru's Cruise Credentials Are Growing

New Mangalore Port, India's seventh-largest cargo port and the only major port on Karnataka's coastline, has been quietly building its cruise tourism profile. The 2025–26 season has emerged as its strongest since before the pandemic, with multiple international cruise calls between December and May.

The port welcomed the Bahamas-flagged MS Island Sky in February 2026, carrying around 100 passengers on a west coast itinerary. Seven Seas Mariner also called at the port in April 2026. Port officials report higher per-passenger onshore spending compared with post-pandemic years, particularly on cultural tours, handicrafts, and coastal cuisine.

Infrastructure upgrades are supporting this growth. The port authority has enhanced immigration and customs areas, improved wayfinding systems, and added visitor amenities. Plans for a dedicated cruise terminal are in the works. Beyond the port, Mangaluru Smart City Mission projects — including riverfront improvements and better connectivity to beaches like Tannirbavi — are expected to make shore excursions more seamless.

India's Cruise Market: Small but Accelerating

India's overnight ocean and coastal cruise industry was valued at just ₹732 crore in FY25, according to a CRISIL report cited in Waterways Leisure Tourism's prospectus. Cordelia commands roughly 79 per cent of that market by value, making it the category's undisputed leader.

The company reported revenue of ₹580 crore in FY26, with EBITDA margins of 20 per cent and net profit of ₹52 crore. Average ticket prices stood at ₹10,980 per passenger, with revenue per passenger per day at ₹12,036. Occupancy dipped to 85 per cent from 91.6 per cent the previous year, which management attributed partly to the India-Pakistan tensions and flight disruptions.

The central government is betting on cruise tourism as a growth driver under its Cruise Bharat Mission. Shipping Minister Sarbananda Sonowal has outlined plans to increase cruise vessel arrivals from 208 in 2023 to 500 by 2030, with passenger volumes projected to rise from 9.5 lakh to 45 lakh by 2047. Twenty-seven new cruise terminals are planned across India's coastline, including facilities at Diu, Puri, Kolkata, and Visakhapatnam.

What It Means for the Diaspora

For the Indian diaspora, Cordelia's expansion opens new possibilities for vacation travel that combines familiar cultural touchpoints with the convenience of cruising. The line's Indian-centric onboard experience — Bollywood-style entertainment, Indian cuisine spanning Jain and vegetarian options, and cricket on deck — is designed to appeal to NRI travellers seeking a homecoming experience at sea. Visa-free domestic sailings and emerging international routes to Sri Lanka, Southeast Asia, and potentially Australia add further appeal.

Mangaluru, with its deep roots in the Konkan and Tulu diaspora communities, could become a particularly compelling embarkation point for travellers with family ties to coastal Karnataka.

Execution Risks Remain

The expansion is not without challenges. Analysts have flagged the leap from a single-vessel operation to a three-ship fleet as Cordelia's central execution risk. The IPO was priced at 112 times trailing earnings — far above global cruise peers that trade at 12–36 times — reflecting a valuation that already assumes successful fleet integration.

Whether Mangaluru materialises as a regular port of call will depend on infrastructure readiness and demand absorption. But with New Mangalore Port already positioning itself as a culturally rich alternative to India's mega-city cruise gateways, and Cordelia actively scouting new ports for its expanded fleet, the pieces for a Mangaluru cruise corridor are falling into place.
